brief: A utensil holder with two bins that is waterproof and dishwasher safe.

requirements.evidence: Two adjacent base cells (piece at 0,0,0 and 1,0,0) built as a small holder, with lockJoints applied and capOpenFaces closing the outer side faces. check_build is clean (no issues, meshClash clear).
Two hex-bin-full bins: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full, one in each cell.

The configurator checks fit and collisions only; it cannot verify waterproofing. Capping the side faces helps the shape, but no sealing, gasket, or material property is modelled, so this cannot be claimed. Drain or pill-hole bin variants were deliberately not used.
Dishwasher safety depends on the printed material and process, which the configurator does not model. Nothing in the build can be verified for it; the material choice is the user's.

finish.summary: Built a two-cell utensil holder with one full-depth bin in each cell, joints locked and open side faces capped; the configurator reports no issues and a clear mesh check. I did not add lids, so the top is open for utensils. Waterproofing and dishwasher safety are material and process properties the configurator cannot check, so those two requirements are unmet and would need to be settled by the material and print choice.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
